body:
WHAT
EnterWorktree creates a git worktree (a second checkout of the same repo) at .magentra/worktrees/<name> on a new branch magentra/<name>, then moves the session working directory into it so later tools operate there. The base commit follows settings.worktree.baseRef: 'fresh' branches from origin's default branch (or HEAD if there is no remote), 'head' from the current HEAD. Names are checked per path segment (A-Za-z0-9._-, no '.' or '..'). With 'path' it switches into an existing worktree instead. It refuses outside a git repo or when a worktree session is already active.

WHY
Without it, experimental work would land in the main checkout, and without name validation a name like '../x' could escape the worktrees folder.

WHERE
engine/tools/src/worktree.ts — enterWorktreeTool (enterSchema with name/path refine), execute(): setCwd presence check, `active` WeakMap check, git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree, path variant via worktreePaths()/normalizePath(), name variant: validateName(), randomName(), baseRef from session.worktreeBaseRef, git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD, git worktree add <dir> -b magentra/<name> <base>, session.setCwd(dir). git() helper wraps execFile. setCwd is implemented in engine/core/src/runtime/session.ts (emits cwd_changed).

TEST CHECKLIST
1. In a temp git repo with one commit (no remote), a fake session with setCwd recording calls and worktreeBaseRef 'fresh', execute EnterWorktree { name: 'feat/x' }; assert .magentra/worktrees/feat/x exists, `git worktree list` includes it, `git branch --list magentra/feat/x` is non-empty, setCwd was called with that dir, and content mentions 'base HEAD'.
2. Add a remote with refs/remotes/origin/HEAD pointing at origin/main that is one commit behind HEAD; with baseRef 'fresh' assert the new worktree's HEAD equals origin/main; with baseRef 'head' assert it equals the repo HEAD.
3. Execute with names 'a/../b', 'a//b', 'bad name', and a 65-char name; assert each returns isError:true before any git command runs (no worktree created).
4. Execute in a temp dir that is not a git repo; assert isError with 'requires a git repository'; execute with a session lacking setCwd; assert isError mentioning 'setCwd'.
5. Enter a worktree, then call EnterWorktree again; assert isError 'already active'; execute { path: 'does/not/exist' } and assert isError 'not a registered git worktree' listing the known ones.
